note: Submodule of mailchimp_transactional. Defines the config entity type mailchimp_transactional_template (class Entity\TemplateMap), config prefix mailchimp_transactional_template.mailchimp_transactional_template.<id>, exported fields id,label,template_name,content_area,only_use_merge_vars,mailsystem_key. Admin route mailchimp_transactional_template.admin at admin/config/services/mailchimp_transactional/templates; permission 'administer mailchimp transactional templates'. A ServiceProvider overrides mailchimp_transactional.service with TemplateService, which matches a Template Map (exact <module>_<key>, then <module>, then default-system) and sends via the API sendTemplate(), else falls back to the base send. Templates live in the external Mailchimp account, so all medium/hard cases are grounded ONLY in the local Template Map config entities: setup/reset write known maps, verify/introspection read them back.

evals.prompt: What does the mailchimp_transactional_template submodule let me do, and what config entity does it use to connect Drupal mail to a Mailchimp template?
evals.expected_output: It lets you wrap Drupal's outgoing email in a Mailchimp Transactional template by creating Template Map config entities (mailchimp_transactional_template) that link a module/mail-key (or default-system) to a template_name and the editable content_area where the Drupal email body is injected.

evals.prompt: Which fields does a Mailchimp Transactional Template Map store, and how does the module decide which map applies to a given email?
evals.expected_output: A Template Map stores id, label, template_name, content_area, only_use_merge_vars, and mailsystem_key. At send time it matches the mailsystem_key against the exact <module>_<key>, then the bare <module>, then a 'default-system' map (mailchimp_transactional_template_load_by_mailsystem), and sends via the API sendTemplate() if a map is found.

evals.prompt: How does the mailchimp_transactional_template module actually change how emails are sent, and what happens if no template map matches a message?
evals.expected_output: Its ServiceProvider overrides the base mailchimp_transactional.service with TemplateService. On send, TemplateService looks up a matching Template Map and, if found, calls the API sendTemplate() injecting the body into content_area; if no map matches it delegates back to the base Service::send() (a plain, non-templated send).

evals.prompt: This site has a Mailchimp Transactional Template Map configured as the site-wide default. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which Mailchimp template name it uses and which content area the email body is placed into.
evals.expected_output: The mtt_default Template Map (mailsystem_key default-system) uses template_name 'welcome-brand' and injects the body into content_area 'main_content'.

evals.prompt: For the Mailchimp Transactional Template Map on this site, inspect the live configuration: does it apply to one specific module/mail-key, or to the whole site by default?
evals.expected_output: It applies site-wide by default: the mtt_default Template Map has mailsystem_key = 'default-system', so it is used for any mail sent through Mailchimp Transactional that has no more specific map.

evals.prompt: Using the mailchimp_transactional_template module, configure this site so that all Mailchimp Transactional email uses the Mailchimp template named 'newsletter' by default. Create a site-wide (default-system) Template Map pointing at the 'newsletter' template and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A mailchimp_transactional_template config entity exists with mailsystem_key = 'default-system' and template_name = 'newsletter' (created via the storage/entity API or the admin form at admin/config/services/mailchimp_transactional/templates).

evals.prompt: There is an existing Mailchimp Transactional Template Map 'mtt_edit' but its content area is set to a placeholder. Change that Template Map so the Drupal email body is injected into the template's 'body_region' editable content area, and apply it to the live site.
